body: @michalszynkiewicz if you haven't started looking at this one, I can take a look tomorrow
I'll likely have a look today or tomorrow

I can reproduce this, however I don't see anything in RESTEasy Reactive or the Reactive REST Client that could be causing it.
@jponge @cescoffier I have a reproducer here: https://github.com/geoand/quarkus-quickstarts/tree/quarkus-17145/rest-client-reactive-quickstart (just start the `rest-client-reactive-quickstart` application in that branch and hit `http://localhost:8080/country/name-uni/us`)

Mind taking a look to see if this is a Mutiny bug or just a misuse of the API? 
When debugging I saw that `UniRetryAtMost#onFailure` was being called, but without the actual operation being retried.

the report doesn't mention reactive anywhere, so I'm guessing both clients suffer from it.

FYI, in Quarkus 2.0 it should be possible to use `@Retry` on methods with Mutiny result types

Sure, but this case seems to me like it should just work.

Also, looking at the stacktrace, it does look like OP used the reactive stack (as did I when I tested Quarkus from main)

After talking with @michalszynkiewicz I am wondering if this is due to the fact that at a low level, a `CompletableFuture` is used by the client to track the result of HTTP call.
Could that be the reason why `retry` doesn't seem to have the desired effect @jponge @cescoffier ?

according to the [REST client documentation](https://quarkus.io/guides/rest-client#async-support)

> When returning a Uni, every subscription invokes the remote service. It means you can re-send the request by re-subscribing on the Uni, or use a retry[...]

so I assume that it must have been working at some point.

> the report doesn't mention reactive anywhere, so I'm guessing both clients suffer from it.
> 
> FYI, in Quarkus 2.0 it should be possible to use `@Retry` on methods with Mutiny result types

It seems like a handy workaround for some cases but in our case we need to be able to programmatically set the amount of retires, waiting duration, etc. with each request.
